purpose: One extracted result or contextual claim per record. Claims are the auditable bridge from source records to review prose.

claims.result_statement: The standard art-gallery decision problem is exists-R-complete, even for simple polygons with integer-coordinate vertices.
claims.locator: Theorem 1, Journal of the ACM 69(1), Article 4, p. 4:2; membership proof in Theorem 13, p. 4:12.
claims.translation_note: Use as modern complexity context only. It does not contradict extremal upper bounds for restricted orthogonal or lattice classes.
limitations: The claim concerns the decision/optimization complexity of finding a guard set, not a worst-case extremal upper bound.
non_implications: Does not rule out sharp universal counting theorems for restricted orthogonal, polyomino, or lattice-normalized models.

claims.result_statement: Every orthogonal polyhedron with e total edges and r reflex edges is guardable by floor((e+r)/12) open edge guards; using the e/r/genus relation gives open-edge-guard bounds of (11/72)e - g/6 - 1 and (7/12)r - g + 1.
claims.locator: Theorem 5, PDF pp. 5-6; Corollaries 6-7, PDF p. 6; Theorem 2, PDF pp. 3-4, for the e/r/genus relation; Theorem 4, PDF pp. 4-5, for the open/closed edge-guard comparison.
claims.translation_note: This is a 3D edge-guard result, not a point-guard or perimeter result. The (7/12)r expression is parameterized by the number of reflex edges; it is not a theorem using only reflex-edge guards.
limitations: The formal bound is stated for open edge guards guarding the open polyhedron model.
The paper relates open and closed edge guards, but the main floor((e+r)/12) and corollary bounds should not be restated as closed-edge-guard theorems without that comparison.
non_implications: Does not prove the Urrutia m/12 + O(1) closed-edge-guard conjecture.
Does not settle general reflex-edge-only guard conjectures for orthogonal polyhedra.

claims.result_statement: A hole-free polyomino with lattice perimeter ell can be guarded by at most max(1, floor(ell/6)) point guards; equivalently, floor(ell/6) guards suffice for ell >= 6, and the comb construction shows the bound is tight.

assumptions: The paper's default convention is that polyominoes and rectilinear art galleries do not contain holes unless otherwise stated.

claims.locator: Theorem 1, journal p. 570; proof in Section 4, journal pp. 572-575; tight comb example in Fig. 3 and following paragraph, journal p. 575.
claims.translation_note: This is the central perimeter-over-six theorem. The source's default convention excludes holes unless otherwise stated, so Theorem 1 covers hole-free integral orthogonal polygons after unit-grid subdivision. It does not prove the hole case.
limitations: The exact theorem is max(1, floor(ell/6)); the shorter floor(ell/6) form is valid for ell >= 6.
Theorem 1 is hole-free under the paper's default convention.
non_implications: Does not prove perimeter-over-six for polyominoes with holes.
Does not by itself settle broader integral-domain conventions that allow holes.

claims.result_statement: Conjecture 6.10 states that, in any rectilinear gallery that may contain holes, the maximum size of a packing of maximal rectangles is an upper bound on the number of guards required; if true, Lemma 6.9 would extend the perimeter-over-six theorem to polyominoes with holes.

assumptions: Chapter 6 uses the no-holes convention unless holes are explicitly mentioned.
The implication to a perimeter bound for holes uses Lemma 6.9 plus Conjecture 6.10.

claims.locator: Chapter 6.3: Theorem 6.3 on thesis p. 67; Lemma 6.9 on thesis p. 72; Conjecture 6.10 and the stated implication for polyominoes with holes on thesis p. 73; Figure 6.6 on thesis p. 73.
claims.translation_note: This is the key source for conditional/open status. The conjecture is a rectangle-packing-to-guard-number statement for rectilinear galleries with holes; perimeter-over-six for polyominoes with holes follows only if that conjecture is true.
limitations: The source explicitly says the author was not able to prove the packing-number upper bound for galleries with holes.
The conjecture is stated for rectilinear galleries with holes, while the perimeter consequence is stated for polyominoes with holes.
non_implications: Does not prove perimeter-over-six for polyominoes with holes.
Does not imply that maximal-rectangle intersection graphs are perfect for galleries with holes; Figure 6.6 gives a one-hole non-perfect example.
